- Switch n port = 1 Broadcast Domain, n Collision Domain

- Switches with VLAN configuration have 4096 - 2 = 4094 VLANs
To conduct a VLAN, the two switches must access 1 VLAN at both ends (10
VLANs require 10 cables to conduct 10 VLANs).
Trunking was born to conduct 4094 VLANs on 1 wire (only costs 1 cable for
Router communication with Switch port trunk
DHCP: Automatic IP allocation feature for a certain VLAN.
⇒ The first condition for DHCP to work is that Routing is completed.
⇒ For DHCP Relay Agent, go to the correct Gateway (where the DHCP
Server configures the Gateway parameters) to point to the DHCP
CDP - LLDP: Used to view device information
Interface VLAN: Usually acts as a Gateway for the entire network.
2-layer model: Interface-vlan is configured at Switch-Core
3-layer model: Interface-vlan is usually configured at Switch-Distribution
When the Switch is connected in a closed loop, a loop phenomenon
will occur. Solution: Temporarily block any port so that the
connection is no longer a closed loop.
Expansion: Switches do not necessarily have to be
the same in terms of equipment, configuration, and port number
Backup: Switches must be the same in terms of device,
Cisco: HSRP Only supports 2 devices ( 1 Active - 1 Standby)
Standard: VRRP Supports up to about 16 devices (1 Active - the rest are Passive)
Solution: Generate 1 virtual GW representing 2 Routers (of which only Active Router is active).
Security Layer2 (originates right from the company)
MAC table attack: overflow the Switch's MAC table (When the Switch overflows the MAC, it will
- Convert Switch into Hub to capture information.
- Causes the Switch to be Down (destructive attack).
- _Solution_: Limit the port speed, and use port Security to limit the number of MACs on a port.
1. MAC learning: default 1 MAC when port Security is enabled
- Static: Assign the MAC address directly to the port
- Dynamic (default): Learn MAC, when reset, learn again -> lose MAC address when Switch resets or
- Sticky: After learning the MAC, it will be saved forever (except when Admin deletes the MAC),
combining learning MAC Dynamically and saving MAC Static.
- Protect: Does not send any information to the administrator, does not affect the port.
- Restrict: Does not affect the port, but does send a warning to the administrator.
- Shutdown: impact the port (err-disable: if you want to enable it again, shut down the port first and
no shutdown again), and send a warning to the administrator.
Attach a SW with the lowest MAC and Priority to the network port (will become the Root Switch),
making all traffic in the network go through this Switch (to capture user information).
→ Affects network access and slows down the network.

- In the Broadcast MultiAccess segment, there will be DR and BDR elections
- DR: undertakes to receive all LSA from the DR-OTHER (224.0.0.5) and return routing
- BDR: only receive LSA from the DR-OTHER (224.0.0.5) and only respond when DR

- Used to filter traffic (Filter) or classify traffic (Classification) in the network according to the
- a. Impact of ACL: Deny and Permit
- Standard: Can only define a single source IP (default destination IP is ANY) --> often used for
- Extended: Definition includes: protocol (ip/icmp/tcp/udp), source IP, destination IP, port-
For example: write ACL to do the following:
- VLAN10: can access the web and ping (the rest cannot be accessed).
- VLAN20: have access to all services.
- VLAN30: prohibit web access and traceroute.
Router(config-acl)#deny ip any any (implicit deny - HIDDEN)
- Source NAT: if >1 then define = ACL
- Destination NAT: if >1 then define = POOL
- Source: n IP-A = 1 -> not defined ACL
- Destination: n IP-B = 1 -> not defined Pool
- b. Dynamic NAT: n IP-A -> n IP-B
Router(config)#ip nat inside source list NAT-1.1-1.12 MY_POOL
- c. NAT overload: n IP-A -> 1 IP-B
- Destination: n IP-B = 1 -> not defined Pool
- 172.16.1.0/24 NAT go out with interface g0/0 connecting to the network
- 172.16.2.0/24 NAT go out with the remaining Public IP 100.0.0.14
Router(config)#ip nat inside source list Internet_1.0 interface g0/0 overload
Router(config)#ip nat inside source list Internet_2.0 100.0.0.14

- VTP has 3 modes: Server (Create VLAN, Sync VLAN),
- Priority: lowest is best (n +/- 4096 apart, default priority Switch = 32768)
- MAC: lowest is best. --> All ports of Root Switch are DP (Designated Port)
- Calculated by Cost: Cost is calculated from the Root Switch to the remaining ports, the lowest
Cost is the best (Root Port - RP).
Step 3: Block port (worst port) - Block all VLANs on this segment.
- Priority of Sender-ID: lowest is best
